subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be warning-only in doctor/config validate, hard validation errors, or left to startup/runtime handling when catalog authority is incomplete?
rationale: The code can enumerate configured refs, but the behavior affects custom providers, forward-compatible model names, fail-closed validation, and upgrade safety, so automation should not choose the contract alone.

options.title: Warning-first validation
options.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config warnings for likely invalid configured refs while distinguishing trusted catalog absence from custom or future model refs without hard-failing existing setups by default.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs during config validation, accepting a compatibility break unless maintainers also define an escape hatch or migration contract.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep config validation permissive and rely on startup warmup, runtime errors, and fallback notices instead of adding a configured-ref analyzer.

recommendation.title: Warning-first validation
recommendation.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config warnings for likely invalid configured refs while distinguishing trusted catalog absence from custom or future model refs without hard-failing existing setups by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses model-selection, config validation, doctor, and compatibility policy surfaces where steipete has the strongest observed ownership signal.
